new.headline: A clean first week back with zero shin pain is exactly the start we wanted. Next week keeps the same three-day pattern and nudges the run intervals a touch longer.

flags.title: Shin response
flags.detail: still the one thing that matters; any ache during a run means stop and we repeat, not progress.

flags.title: Run interval length
flags.detail: moving from short pulses to 2 min of running, so watch how the shin feels the next morning.

flags.title: Total load
flags.detail: weekly minutes up roughly 10 percent, which is the ceiling I want to hold for now.

new.analysis:
The plan holds your Mon / Wed / Sat rhythm and raises the dose in two small ways: each session goes from 15 to about 17 – 18 minutes, and the run blocks grow from short pulses to 2 minutes of running with 1 minute of walking. That lifts weekly moving time from 45 to about 52 minutes, inside the 10 percent step I want to stay under this early.

I am keeping everything easy on purpose. No strides, no hills, no faster running until you have four pain-free weeks stacked up; you have one in the bank, so we are counting carefully. If the shin pipes up at 3/10 or less and settles by morning, we repeat the session rather than add. Above 3/10, or sore the next day, we shorten and I want to hear from you.

Your 30-minutes-continuous target by mid-October is realistic from here. Rough path: this week 2 min run blocks, then 3 min, then 4 – 5 min, then stitching into a continuous 15 – 20 min and growing from there. Keep the physio calf and hip work on the two non-running days; it is doing real work for you.

One small housekeeping note: the Clifton 9s are at 60 km and have plenty of life, but keep an eye on how they feel underfoot as mileage climbs over the next month.
